block.comment: Timer1 generates STEP on D9; DIR uses D4. Connect the TB6600 control inputs according to its input wiring, with common signal ground. Acceleration is 5000 steps/s²; change it here. Timer1 cannot simultaneously run the Timer1/Servo lessons.
Start stopped, then set an exact signed target from Plotter. Upload, connect Plotter at 115200 baud, then Start. The board sends the complete layout and instructions.

Parse a signed whole number from valueStart through the end of the command. Reject empty text, non-digits and oversized values before changing any setting. Each handler also checks its own permitted range and step.
Fixed incoming line buffer, including room for a terminator. Charts, images and the JSON header stay on the computer/Flash, not in this array.

Read one complete newline-terminated command. Partial lines stay in a fixed byte buffer. CR is ignored; oversized commands are discarded. There is no String allocation or waiting for bytes. Expand this reusable function to see the ordinary array and logic blocks.
Confirm the accepted speed. The timer library ramps toward this target.
This is an ordinary Serial text message stored in Flash. Click it to edit formatted JSON. The computer creates instruments and computes derived fields; this sketch sends only input values.
Send the dashboard on boot and Start. Motor stays stopped until a nonzero speed is entered.
Plotter Stop requests zero speed with deceleration.
Initialize the hardware engine but request no motion. Start only announces the dashboard; enter a nonzero speed to move.
Use elapsed milliseconds instead of delay. The command reader remains responsive between updates; unsigned subtraction also works when millis wraps.
The hardware engine plans acceleration and generates pulses in the background. Report the requested target at 10 Hz; no run call or delay is needed.
